characters.name: open/close all folders
characters.description: Catchphrase: "Oh yeah!" follow by them high fiving each other upon reaching school. Chronic Hero Syndrome: They're both good kids at heart and willing to help out where they can. The Cassandra: They try to tell Prudence why they're late, but she never believes them since the stories sound way too outlandish. Turn the Other Cheek: They're not one to hold grudges against some of the oddities that try to harm or take advantage of them. Even helping them out afterward. Weirdness Magnet: Craziness just attracts to the two like flies. Even they aren't sure why that is.

characters.name: Nate
characters.description: Book Dumb: Hinted at, he's not a dunce but it's implied he doesn't take his studies as seriously as he should. Dub Name Change: In the original French version, his name is Oscar. Forced Transformation: Gets hit with this often if it isn't given to him willingly. He got turned into a frog when trying to help a man bewitched by a witch and got turned into a werewolf when scratched by one. Jumped at the Call: If there's something worth exploring, he'll instantly go for the chance to check it out. Losing a Shoe in the Struggle: Happened to him in "The Ring" (had to slip out of shoes that were caught in cement in order to dive in front of a incoming steamroller to reverse the ring's bad luck), "The Magic Shoes" (being freed of the shoes after they were beaten in a race) and "The Werewolf" (Lost his shoes when the werewolf transformation reached its peak).

characters.name: Malika
characters.description: Action Girl: Not a major one but she not one to shy away from going into action when promoted. In the Hood: Wears a hoodie and occasionally pulls it up. Letting Her Hair Down: Usually has it in a ponytail. In "The Faun", she lets it down when she was bewitched into partying. Not So Above It All: On some occasions, she can be the catalyst to the episode situation such as "The Magic Shoes" (Forced Nate to put on said shoes which caused him to run endlessly), "The Concert" (Snuck into a rehearsal for a concert because she was a fan of the singer) and "The Unicorn" (Willing to help out said unicorn because she thought it was cute while Nate was suspicious why the unicorn had so many dogs helping her). Passionate Sports Girl: Hinted at. In "The Magic Shoes" she's pretty excited for a Fields Day event at their school and practically forced Nate into coming to compete. In fact, she was the catalyst for episode when she had Nate put on someone else's running shoes when Nate "claimed" he forgot his.

characters.name: Principal Prudence
characters.description: Catchphrase: "Nate and Malika. Late again, I see." Or some variation. Crazy-Prepared: In "The Magic Shoes", she reveals she has some spare running shoes just in case someone forgets theirs to Nate's dismay. As she puts it...Prudence: Well lucky for you, I'm prudence by name and prudence by nature. Not So Above It All: Acts like a strict school marm, but is prone to some silly actions too. Prim and Proper Bun: Wears this as her default hairstyle. Reasonable Authority Figure: She's willing to overlook the two's tardiness on some occasions if they have proof to back up their claims or sharing some wise bit of wisdom.

characters.name: Maurice
characters.description: A Day in the Spotlight: "The Cave Girl" focuses on him since said cave girl takes a liking to him. Likewise "The Dinosaur" when he gets turns into a t-Rex. Big Damn Heroes: It's his negative side that helps Nate and Malike reclaim the camera in "The Flash". Forced Transformation: Gets accidentally turned into a Tyrannosaurs Rex in "The Dinosaur". Headphones Equal Isolation: Usually always milling about listening to something on his headphones. Hidden Depths: If his negative side in "The Flash" is any indication, he would like to be a dancer.

characters.name: Terry
characters.description: A Day in the Spotlight: "The Cuddly Toy" is more focused on him as said toy belongs to Terry and doesn't want to leave him just yet despite the others of the toy store trying to force him too. He's also the cause of the events in "The Flash". Big Bad: The villain of the "The Flash" largely due to being separated from his negative side which is overly nice while making his mean-ness worst. The Bully: Always hassling Nate and Malika over something or other, as you do. Pet the Dog: He vouches for Nate and Malika at the end of "The Cuddly Toy" and "The Flash" on why they're late. Real Men Wear Pink: He still loves his plush toy even if he's older now.

characters.name: Dwayne
characters.description: Arson, Murder, and Jaywalking: He takes any offense very seriously, even littering. Badbutt: He always makes a lot of erratic movements. Sometimes even making his finger into a gun motion. Beware the Silly Ones: He's a bit of ham but the man is dedicated to his job.

characters.name: Cosmo
characters.description: Accidental Misnaming: He never gets Nate and Malika's names right. Bazaar of the Bizarre: His stand has all sorts of stuff within, conveniently having whatever Nate and Malika need when they come to him. Cloudcuckoolander: A bit out of sorts it would seem.

characters.name: Violet
characters.description: Beehive Hairdo: Has this hairstyle, with even a few leaves sticking out of her hair. Heck it's so huge it ended up busting a hole in her bee suit's helmet. Caring Gardener: She takes her job pretty serious and was actually distraught at one point when an old tree had to be torn down due to withering. She likewise was overjoyed when it showed signs of life which prevented its demolition Competition Freak: “The Blooming City” reveals that she used to be uber-competitive at darts until she found that nobody would play with her anymore, so she gave up and took up gardening instead. Unfortunately, a flower-growing contest rekindles that spark, so much so that she starts turning people into topiaries. Transflormation:In “The Spores”, she becomes infected with the spores of a rareorcus parasiticus, which start turning her into a shrub.“The Blooming City” has her using specially-engineered seeds to turn people into flower bushes. In “The Spores”, she becomes infected with the spores of a rareorcus parasiticus, which start turning her into a shrub.

characters.name: Mrs. Rainford & Ajax
characters.description: Beehive Hairdo: Despite looking like a hat, that's really her hair on her head. Mr. Muffykins: She treats Ajax this way. Running Gag: Her talking with Melodie with the latter barely even listening. Serious Business: Proper manners, she ends up holding up Nate and Malika in "The Watch" because they needed Melody to tell them where to find something in a hurry, interrupting Mrs. Rainford's conversation with her.

characters.name: Professor Toybos
characters.description: A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Had this happen to himtwice, once in "The Cyborgs" (the A.I reasoned machines were superior and started replacing people in town) and "The Robot" (Said robot turning on him when considered dismantling him due to old age). Bungling Inventor: His inventions have a habit of not working right or turning on him. Gave Up Too Soon: In "The Insects" he actually manages to invent aShrink Raybut figured it didn't work right and had it thrown out on garbage day. Nate and Malika got affected by it and manage to get it working properly...right in time for the local garbage man to come pick it up before they could tell the professor. Though he uses the same device in "The Spore" so they either eventually did inform him and he retrieved it or he just built another one.

characters.name: Melodie
characters.description: Ambiguously Human: "The Card Collector" has said collector claiming that she was a card of warrior woman given human form. Nothing is really confirmed at the end of the episode. Running Gag:Something happening to her bike and Nate and Malika having to deliver whatever mail she was going to.Her talking with Mrs. Rainford with Melodie barely even listening. Something happening to her bike and Nate and Malika having to deliver whatever mail she was going to. Her talking with Mrs. Rainford with Melodie barely even listening. Gag Nose: Not overly comical but it's pretty noticeable.

characters.name: Maxime Dermy
characters.description: Bald of Evil: He's shown to be bald and not at all a pleasant person. Heel–Face Turn: By the third appearance in season two, he and the kids bury the hatchet after dealing with a big fish in park's local lake. His last appearance shows he genuinely turned over a new leaf. Jerkass: Always on the lookout for rare animal so he can get rich off of. You know it's bad when one of said animals wasSanta's reindeer. Would Hurt a Child: ActivelyfightsNate with acattle prodin "The Dragon'". Likewise, in "The Reindeer", he has no problem with throwing Nate and Malika into one of his cages...with another much more deadly animal.

characters.name: Garbage Goblins
characters.description: Everyone Has Standards: Pimple may like living in garbage, but even he has a limit to how horrible one can smell. Which is the focus of his sequel episode and having to deal with his cousin who smells so horrible, it chased away his family and is literally fogging up the town. Family Man: Pimple is revealed to be one. I Lied: Pimple, the one the duo first meet, claims trolls are scared of humans. The first encounter proves otherwise. Our Goblins Are Different: They live in sewers and love trash.

characters.name: Chloe
characters.description: A Day in the Spotlight: She gets her own episode in "The Wedding Dress". Calling the Old Man Out: She ends up putting her foot down after her mother claims people only like her for her beauty, stating that she can decide for herself and that Gideon and she truly do love each other. Hair of Gold, Heart of Gold: A nice girl and a blonde to boot. Letting Her Hair Down: Normally has it tied up in braids due to their length, she let's if flow when going to help Gideon, Nate and Malika.

characters.name: Ramona
characters.description: Big Bad: Of "The Enchanted Frog". Blind Without Them: Nate manages to swipe her glasses, giving her fuzzy vision. Crazy-Prepared: Put an extra spell on Gideon in case anyone tried the "Princess kissing frog to break the spell" trick as Nate found out the hard way. Foil: To Gisette and Hazel. While initially starting antagonistic and more then happy to wield her magic if pressed. She's more disciplined of the three and and mostly just stern. She also doesn't have any hostility to the duo after her introduction episode. Hoist by His Own Petard: Gets hit with her own magic spell and turned into a frog herself. Also counts asLaser-Guided Karma.

characters.name: Gisette
characters.description: Creating Life: She desired a child an created a Gingerbread Man to have one, though he's a bit unruly at first and it takes awhile for him to come around to seeing her as a parent. Foil: To Ramona and Hazel. Compared to the two, she's the nicest of the three witches and doesn't abuse her magic. Though she likewise doesn't seem to be much of a spellcaster in the first place. Token Good Teammate: Shows herself as such in "The Witch-Con", being the only witch willing to help Nate and Malika clear their names after they're framed for a magic mishap.

characters.name: Asgore
characters.description: Everyone Hates Math: A major punishment in his timeline is that the robotic enforcers of the school put the student through solving math problems 24/7. Even worse in the detention room where they put the students on bikes while doing so, with the bikes picking up speed for every wrong answer. Kid from the Future: The episode is even titled after the trope. Unlike most examples though, he's not related to Nate or Malika. Set Right What Once Went Wrong: His goal in his episode. He seems to have succeeded but Nate and Malika entering the time portal behind him ends up setting off the chain of events anyway. After the time trip through, they manage...though Nate does let slip to Prudence about how the future school will be andshe has a thoughtful look on her face. Shout-Out: He travels through time by connecting a deviceto his hoverboard.

characters.name: Hazel
characters.description: Body Surf: Switches bodies frequently in "The Enchanted Bracelet", including Nate and Malika. Disproportionate Retribution: Turns Nate and Malika old just for accidently bumping into her while running past her. The pair even apologized for it but she felt they needed to learn a lesson regardless. Foil: To Ramona and Gisette. Of the three, she'smorethen happy to use her powers with impunity and for her own benefit and amusement to the detriment of others. Fitting theWicked Witcharchetype much better of the three witches and each encounter with the duo is usually antagonistic. Grand Theft Me: Hazel pulls this on Maurice in her second appearance via a magic bracelet, taking his body while sticking him in hers. And doing so multiple times with others as well Karma Houdini: She gets away with her actions in "Grandpa". She does restore Nate and Malika to their rightful ages in the end, but only onherterms.

characters.name: Zimbra
characters.description: A.I. Is a Crapshoot: Was meant to help the professor but turned malicious when she saw humanity as weak. Big Bad: Of "The Cyborgs" & "The Glitch". Capture and Replicate: Her main goal in which she sleep gasses her victims, scans them and makes a robotic duplicate to replace them with. Creepy Monotone: Speaks this way through her duplicates, even the male ones. Take Over the World: Her ultimate goal with her schemes.

characters.name: Miracle Girl
characters.description: And Then What?: She runs into this problem in "Miracle Girl Blues", having defeated Gigantix, she doesn't know what to do with her free time. Brought Down to Normal: If she doesn't have her headband, she can't use her powers. Flight: Gains the power to fly due to her headband. MacGuffin: Her headband. Nate gets a hold of it for awhile and Gigantix wants it to enact his plans. Mind Over Matter: The main power of her headband allows her to enhance her mental capabilities so that she can levitate objects.

characters.name: Gigantix
characters.description: A Twinkle in the Sky: Miracle Girl throws him into a storage closet thenthrows that into outer space. He's still up there in "The Alphabet Agency", communicating with a mole within to undermine Miracle Girl. Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: When he calls his minions to merge with him, he grows much bigger. Big Bad: Of "The Superhero". Blob Monster: He is a red gooey blob monster. Colony Drop: His planned involved crashing a space station into the Earth to show how much of a serious threat he was and make the world leaders surrender to him.

characters.name: Boris & Clementine
characters.description: Big Bad: Both in "The Mummy" & Boris in "The Golden Crown". Blatant Lies: Boris claims he's security when Nate stumbles upon him. Then Clementine walks by with a bag of stolen jewels in her hands, giving them away. Even Evil Has Standards: In "The Golden Crown", Clementine notices how dangerous the crown's power is getting and how power mad Boris is becoming. She tries to convince him to give up the power and it's only when she gets turned into a statue that he finally realizes. Fat and Skinny: Their dynamic with Boris being the latter and Clementine being the former. Hoist by His Own Petard: Trapped underneath the t-Rex skeleton they had brought to life with the relic to attack Nate, Malika and Pashoot with.

characters.name: Pat
characters.description: Alternate Identity Amnesia: She doesn't remember what happens when her wolf instincts overcome her. However, at the end of the episode, this stops being a problem, as she becomes able to control her wolf form. Our Werewolves Are Different: She was apparently born into lycanthropy as she mentions being part of a clan. Also she doesn't need the moon to fully transform as she can do so when she smells food. That said, she can transfer the transformation if she scratches or bites anyone. Power Limiter: Her necklace which was given to her by her clan to prevent her transformations while in the daytime. It works on her and only her and losing it causes her to transform at the smell of food. By episodes end, she learns to control her transformation enough to not need it anymore.

characters.name: Atticus
characters.description: Ascend to a Higher Plane of Existence: After beating the head construction worker, he's finally allowed to pass on. Forgot About His Powers: Sometimes keeps forgetting he's a ghost and can't be harmed. Our Ghosts Are Different: Apparently not fighting in a coliseum is enough to get you curse into staying as a ghost within it. Though he can seem to interact with the mortal world. Unfinished Business: Can't pass on till he fights and beats someone in the arena of the coliseum.

characters.name: Kiki
characters.description: Attack of the 50-Foot Whatever: Due to Nate not reading the instructions on the plant growth formula, she grows gargantuan as a result. She's returned to normal size by just watering her since it dilutes the formula within her. Man-Eating Plant: Due to growing huge, she becomes this.

characters.name: Troll
characters.description: Big BadOf "The Garbage Goblins". Real Men Wear Pink: Likes the teddy bear that belonged to one of the Pimple's children. Our Trolls Are Different: As Pimple states, not all trolls live under bridges. Weakened by the Light: Hates sunlight and is defeated when Nate, Malika and the goblins surround it with sunlight reflected off of metal they're holding (along with the flashlight feature on Nate's watch), scaring it off.

characters.name: Dragons
characters.description: Mama Bear: The mother of course doesn't appreciate how Max handled her child. Playing with Fire: Naturally. Malika convinces Nate not to bring the baby one to school for this reason and the mother dragon flames Max's patoot once she gets free.

characters.name: Insects
characters.description: The Cameo: In “The Dream”, human-sized versions of them appear inside Nate’s dream having a tea party. Changed My Mind, Kid: Roach stomps off after Nate saves him from George, Toybus's pet iguana. He leaves in a huff but later comes to help him in the climax of the ep. Dark Is Not Evil: Roach, Flea and Stinkbug come off a little rough but they're friendly once Nate and Malika get to know them (though Roach takes awhile to come around). Heck they warn them to run when George shows up and Flea helps them escape when he see they're too slow at their current size. Spider, who by all rights should be a predator to the former three, is likewise friendly. Even helping Nate down when he gets caught in her web. Fartillery: Stinkbug uses this naturally. A running gag in the ep is that Malika constantly keep running into him when he lets off his smells. Fantastic Racism: Roach isn't very fond of humans.

characters.name: Igor
characters.description: Blatant Lies: Its very obvious he's a thief but Nate falls for it hook link and sinker. Obviously Evil: Shifty eyed, wearing black clothes, hiding from the police. Oh yeah,totally trustworthy. Shout-Out: Voiced likeMaxwell Smart.

characters.name: Haunted House
characters.description: Genius Loci: Naturally being a haunted house. Can bar passages, make steel bars, make brick walls instantly and cause the appliances to come to life. It's only haunted because it wishes to be cleaned. Once it is, it calms down. Haunted House: Again, natch.

characters.name: Howard Bristle
characters.description: Get Out!: Yells this when he hears Nate and Malika enter the house as he doesn't want them to be trapped. Innocent Bystander: He had virtually no idea the house was haunted and gets caught up in it's paranormal clutches. Nice Guy: Very, he helps the duo try to escape the house, helps try to defend them when the appliance attack them, helps clean it when Nate stumbles upon the solution and promises to upkeep it to prevent any more hauntings. Unexpected Inheritance: Never expected to have his aunt leave him a house andcertainlynever realized it was haunted.

characters.name: Shawn
characters.description: Leprechaun: Is one of course. Taken for Granite: Happens to him in the middle of the episode since he lost all his coins. Though Makika manages to revive him by giving him her coins. Thinking Up Portals: He, and other leprechauns, can travel anywhere through portals they can summon. In the season 1 finale, he uses these to quickly bring a large group of allies to Nate and Malika to help out against the alien invaders.

characters.name: Ian
characters.description: Big Bad: Of "The Leprechaun" Disproportionate Retribution: Claims he stole the gold of other leprechaun because apparently they never helped him look for his. Shawn claims hewantedto help but Ian disappeared before he got the chance. Heel–Face Turn: After Shawn saves him from falling into ocean, he is grateful and rekindles their friendship. Even more so when Malika gives him her coins to keep him from turning into a statue when he returns the stolen gold. We Used to Be Friends: Said verbatim by Shawn when explaining who he is.

characters.name: Ms. Principal
characters.description: Big Bad: Of "The Kid from the Future" who rules the future school with an iron fist. Disproportionate Retribution: Pretty much doinganythingin her school nets detention: speaking too loud, wearing the wrong uniforms, roaming the halls looking for the restroom. Logic Bomb: She can only take so much misconduct that it fries her circuits.

characters.name: Romus
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Asgore state he gets detention daily. Jerkass: Our heroes did virtually nothing to him, he just tattled on them to make his punishments easier. Him giving that smug expression after he did the deed doesn't help. The Stool Pigeon: Ratted on Nate, Malika and Asgore when he overheard them talking about trying to retrieve Asgore's hoverboard from the principal's office in order to reduce his detention hours, making completing their objective harder then it needed to be.

characters.name: Mermaids
characters.description: Amazing Technicolor Population: Usually have a variety of muted colors on them. Disproportionate Retribution: Force Nate to fight a trash monster just because he threw some trash into the lake. And even then, it was an accident as it got blown out of his hand and into the water by the wind. Granted, he was briefly going leave it in until Malika gave him a disapproving glare to make him pick it up., but still. Never My Fault: While they blame humans for their situation, it never seems to occur to them to either ask humans to stop dumping trash in the lake or clean it up themselves. Prongs of Poseidon: Admit they only have tridents as their weapons. Sirens Are Mermaids: They're called mermaids with many traits of sirens. They pulled Nate into the lake by using their singing to lure him in. They later use it to keep the trash monster at bay to give the duo time to dismantle it.

characters.name: Trash Monster
characters.description: Big Bad: Of "The Mermaids" Blob Monster: A gooey being entirely made from trash. Nigh-Invulnerability: It can be hurt but will usually put itself back together again. Nate and Malika have to dismantle it piece by piece to stop it. Music Soothes the Savage Beast: The mermaids use their singing to halt it temporarily.

characters.name: Gideon
characters.description: Bewitched Amphibians: As stated, he was cursed by Chloe mother to become a frog. Determinator: Even if he's turned into a frog, it doesn't stop him from trying to reach his true love. Now You Tell Me?: It isn't until after Nate kisses him to bring him back to normal and gets turned into a frog himself that he informs him the witch had expected that and cursed anyone who tried it.

characters.name: Wizimix
characters.description: Beware the Quiet Ones: He's a pretty friendly, if timid, guy., but threaten his friends and he becomesveryintimidating. Cuteness Proximity: Has this effect on most in his regular form. While it's fine with humans, it's considered a disgrace for monsters. Dark Is Not Evil: He doesn't truly wanna scare anyone, least not maliciously and just trying to get his diploma to move on in the world. When he finally does, he states he'll go into pictures to help make horror movies. One-Winged Angel: When the owner/tester of the dark house ride threatens Nate and Malika, this manages to trigger his transformation into a much bigger and deep sounding monster so he can protect them, scaring not only them but said tester. Ironically enough, this impresses her enough to pass him and receive his diploma. Pick on Someone Your Own Size: Says this verbatim when the Scare Examiner threatens Nate and Malika. Ironically dwarfing her in size.

characters.name: Scare Examiner
characters.description: Berserk Button: Liars. Nate claims he was just trying to hide that Wizimix scared him but she's skeptical on that. After allowing a retry, they try to get Maurice to be Wizimix's final exaam target but he fails and they try to claim that Maurice was indeed scared by him. She see right through the lie and nearly attacks Nate and Malika for doing so. Big Bad: Slightly of "The Adorable Monster". She not actively out to stop Nate and Malika and just doing her job. But does threaten them when they ask her to give Wizimix another chance. Didn't See That Coming: When she goes to threaten Nate and Malika, Wizimix manages to tap into his transformation to protect them. Needless to say she's both surprised by his monster form but likewise impressed as well and it's enough to pass him. Ghostly Glide: Moves around in a gliding like motion. Considering her cloak is covering her whole body, it's likely she's not even walking. No Name Given: Her name's never spoken.

characters.name: Genie
characters.description: And I Must Scream: He's been stuck in his lamp with nothing to do but read books until someone comes along and rubs the lamp to grant their wishes. Kinda understandable why he was desperate to get out. Exact Words: Uses this to try and free himself from the lamp initially. I Just Want to Be Free: Wants to be free of the lamp once and for all. Despite nearly getting Nate to take his place, Malika and he are willing to help him and succeed by having Mrs. Rainford wish him free. Never My Fault: Claims Nate and Malika were only interested in their wishes then freeing him. However Nate only used one wish and would've likely wished him free if he hadn't tricked him. Jackass Genie: He grants Nate's first wish to have muscles. But when the wish doesn't work out as intended, he takes Nate's statement that "I wish I was back as the way I was" as "Turn him back into a baby" making him waste his second wish. Since Nate isn't really aware of his situation in that state, the genie tricks Nate into wishing thathewas the genie in order to free himself and get Nate to take his place.

characters.name: Levvia
characters.description: Action Girl: A warrior princess even. She quickly demonstrates it by fighting two of the villain's henchmen when Nate and Malika arrive in the book world. The Beastmaster: Demonstrate this when a lioness is forced to attack Nate, Malika and her. She manages to calm it down and remove the magic thorn in her paw, bringing the lioness back to normal. Face Death with Dignity: When Malika reveals what's meant to happen to her, she was more then willing to go along with it to save her animal friends. But Nate and Malika convince her otherwise. The Hero Dies: Initially, the book ended with her stopping the villain but dying in the process to do so. Heroic Sacrifice: Initially dies while pulling the villain to his own demise.

characters.name: King Aria
characters.description: Aristocrats Are Evil: As stated, he's an evil king whose willing to destroy the Savannah wildlife just for his own selfish ends. Big Bad: AShow Within a Showexample. He's this within Levia's story as well of "The Magic Book" in general. It's All About Me: Doesn't care that he's taking water from the wildlife. Just that'll look good within his castle. Making a Splash: With his magic specter, he fights Aria with water blasts. Rampage from a Nail: Invoked; he controls a lioness by implanting a magical thorn into its paw, and sends it to attack those he doesn’t like (read:Levvia).

characters.name: Santa Claus
characters.description: Bad Butt: Makes a lot of erratic movement and "cloaking" himself with the surroundings while looking for his reindeer. Badass Biker: Has this motif, his sled is designed like a motorbike. Tan Lines: Due to wearing goggles while flying, he has these over his face when he removes them.

characters.name: Brian
characters.description: Flight: Naturally, though in this case it's magic dust that helps him. Gag Nose: A blue nosed reindeer Non-Human Sidekick: To Santa. Shout-Out: Hmm, a blue nosed reindeer?Wouldn't happen to know certain pirate doctor, would he? The Voiceless: Unlike most examples, he doesn't speak.

characters.name: Winkle
characters.description: British Accents: Speaks in a Scottish accent. Cowardly Lion: He reveals he was meant to take test involving a Chimera but chickened out by time traveling. And does it again when cornered by the creature, warping Nate, Malika and him into the past to escape it only to bring it with them. Ultimately when put on the spot, he eventually decides to man up and take the beast on by himself. Nice Job Breaking It, Hero!: In trying to get the Chimera to go away, he accidentally gives itthe ability to breathe fire. Tired of Running: After his spell book is destroyed by flames and Nate and Malika are about to be fried. He decides to stop running and fight the Chimera.

characters.name: Zinyak
characters.description: Glamour: Has a device that he uses to make himself look normal. They later weaponize it when Zinyak's bodyguard comes looking for him and Nate tricks said guard with it. I Just Want to Be Normal: While he doesn't mind being royalty, he likewise just wants to have fun every now and then. Heck he finds the idea of going toschoolinteresting. Though he admits he's home-schooled and never got a chance to interact with others. Octopoid Aliens: His true form is that of a one eyed octopus like alien. Royal Blood: Revels he's a prince of his planet with his father being the king. The Runaway: Reveals he's really royalty but ran away from home to avoid to avoid the strict scheduling he had to go through on his home planet.

characters.name: Zinyak's father
characters.description: Good All Along: Framed as aBig Badof the episode, he's actually quite benevolent and just looking for his son out of worry. Good Parents: Just wants what's best for his son and trying to prepare him for when he has to take the throne. Octopoid Aliens: Same as his son. Reasonable Authority Figure: After hearing both his son as well as Nate and Malika out, he agrees to ease up on his Zinyak's tutoring and allows him a day to hang with Nate and Malika at school.

characters.name: Bunny Numbins
characters.description: Animate Inanimate Object: A living toy as the title of the episode stated. British Accent: Another Irish accented speaker. Puppy-Dog Eyes: Uses this in order to convince Nate to help her. Undying Loyalty: To Terry. She knows she'll have to leave him someday, but likewise knows it isn't the time yet and that he doesn't mean what he says. Trying desperately to convince the council of that fact.

characters.name: Elfax
characters.description: A.I. Is a Crapshoot: A little better then Sibra at least since Elfax at least had a reason to turn on the Professor. Big Bad: Of "The Robot" Crazy-Prepared: Nate, Malika and Toybus try to initially stop him by taking out the battery on his back. However once Nate does so, he reactivates. Revealing he had a second one installed in himself just in case. Determinator: Even when Nate, Malika and Toybus stop his plan the first time. He goes to Plan B, which is to overload the city's power grid and shut down all the appliances within. Freudian Excuse: As stated in his description, he went evil when the Professor considered scrapping him.

characters.name: Queen Pashoot
characters.description: But Now I Must Go: Once the relic is returned, she willingly returned back to her slumber with Malika telling Nate it's kind of a "journey" for her and the events of the episode interrupted it. Cute Monster Girl: Actually looks quite adorable. Dark Is Not Evil: Despite her appearance, she reveals herself to be friendly. Glowing Eyes: When she's revived, her eyes are glowing green. Go Out with a Smile: When Nate and Malika first see her on display, she has a frown on her face. When she returns back to her dormant state, she's smiling.

characters.name: The Negatives
characters.description: Apologizes a Lot: Negative Terry does this a lot for his actions. Big Damn Heroes: Negative Maurice ends up saving the camera after it's nearly dropped trying to get it away from Terry. Deadpan Snarker: Negative Malika is pretty sarcastic at everything the duo do. Deliberately Monochrome: As they're negatives, the have a monochrome tint to them. Go Out with a Smile: When the camera’s effect is reversed and all the negatives vanish back into the people they split off from, Nice Terry is seen smiling as his body dissolves. However, Terry’s sudden uncharacteristic behavior at the episode’s ending may imply that his duplicate isn’t really gone.

characters.name: King Edward
characters.description: A Child Shall Lead Them: He's already a king despite being an elementary school aged child. Identical Stranger: He and Nate could be identical twins. King Incognito: attempts to ditch his crown and hide after he learns someone is plotting to kidnap him. Nate then finds the crown and is mistaken for Edward. Royal Brat: Very selfish and likes to boss people around. He gets better near the end of the episode.

characters.name: Suzie
characters.description: Action Girl: It turns out she's secretly is one being a Valkyrie, she just isn't interested in the warrior lifestyle. The season three finale,Nate Without Malika, shows her in full action mode when the pair arrived in the dystopian altered timeline. Ambiguously Human: In "The Valkyries", she's actually a Valkyrie herself. Ascended Extra: Mostly just a background extra who, sometimes briefly, gets involved in some of the weirdness of the show. Season three gives her more of a character. The Runaway: She actually hails from another dimension of Valkyries, but came to like living on Earth and wanted to live as a human. However the events of "The Valkyries" had them track her down for her test and force her back home. Luckily Nate and Malika follow after her and help her out.

characters.name: Fahim
characters.description: And I Must Scream: He's been stuck in his lamp with nothing to do but read books until someone comes along and rubs the lamp to grant their wishes. Kinda understandable why he was desperate to get out. Exact Words: Uses this to try and free himself from the lamp initially. I Just Want to Be Free: Wants to be free of the lamp once and for all. Despite nearly getting Nate to take his place, Malika and he are willing to help him and succeed by having Mrs. Rainford wish him free. Never My Fault: Claims Nate and Malika were only interested in their wishes then freeing him. However Nate only used one wish and would've likely wished him free if he hadn't tricked him. Jackass Genie: He grants Nate's first wish to have muscles. But when the wish doesn't work out as intended, he takes Nate's statement that "I wish I was back as the way I was" as "Turn him back into a baby" making him waste his second wish. Since Nate isn't really aware of his situation in that state, the genie tricks Nate into wishing thathewas the genie in order to free himself and get Nate to take his place.

characters.name: Jumbo
characters.description: Disney Death:In “The Return of the Cuddly Toys”, spending too long without a child to love him reverts him to an inanimate object, but he comes back to life again once he’s in the hands of his former kid. Heel–Face Revolving Door: In his first appearance, he was an antagonistic but well-meaning leader who was only opposed to Nate and Malika because they weren’t supposed to know about toys being alive, but then realized they were genuinely helpful. And then in his second appearance he goes full evil and tries to take over Christmas,only to be revealed to be doing it for the toy equivalent of aFreudian Excuse, and turn good again when he’s reunited with his now-grown owner. Living Toys: A stuffed toy elephant. Named After Somebody Famous: He’s blatantly named after the circus elephant Jumbo. Tragic Abandoned Toy: Suffered from having his kid grow up and leave him, motivating him to try and steal Christmas in his second appearence.His kid is now Principal Prudence, and when she gets him back at the end of the episode she’s so overjoyed that she doesn’t even bother punishing Nate and Malika for tardiness.

characters.name: Snow Fairy
characters.description: Harmless Freezing: Everyone she freezes in ice crystals turns out fine once they’re thawed out. Heel–Face Turn: She initially wants to freeze everyone as retribution for being trapped in a snow globe, but changes her mind once Nate and Malika make her realize that, with everyone around locked in ice, she’ll be just as lonely as she was in the globe. Hidden Depths: A late Season 3 episode reveals that she can sing hard rock and play (magically-summoned) electric guitar. An Ice Person: Can do things like freeze a whole town solid and create a massive ice palace. Logical Weakness: Her ice powers won’t work against sources of heat; even a small battery-powered hair dryer is enough to keep her from freezing Nate and Malika.

characters.name: Ivan
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: A living gingerbread man a la the fairy tale. The Runaway: In his introductory episode, he runs away from Gisette, feeling that she’s overprotective and wanting to see the world. Super-Speed: True to the fairy tale, you reallycan’tcatch him.

characters.name: Garrett
characters.description: Heel–Face Turn: Ed and Nate eventually help him realize just how cruel he’s being, and he vows to change for the better. Perverse Puppet: Has a very cruel sense of humor, and can take control of his handler’s body to force them to go along with his pranks. He gets better at the end of the episode, though.

characters.name: Chromapix
characters.description: Action Girl: The two that appear in “The Chromapix”, Carmine and Captain Ultraviolet, are both female butt-kickers. All Crimes Are Equal: In “The Necropix”, Captain Ultraviolet goes crazy and starts declaring that anything bearing the colors of “their enemy”- that is, black and grey- should be destroyed and recolored; Malika gets sent to an asteroid prison for wanting her hair to remain black. Black-and-White Insanity: Literally in “The Necropix”, as they start trying to eliminate the color grey from the universe. Coloring in the World: They wield lasers modeled after paintbrushes that can restore color to objects greyed out by a Necropix, or recolor already-colored objects. Don't Look At Me: Shouted by Captain Ultraviolet when the bandage hiding her “wound” (actually a small area on her stomach greyed by a Necropix’s attack) falls off.

characters.name: Necropix
characters.description: A later episode, “The Necropix”, reveals that most of them aren’t actually evil, and introduces a cute little Necropix kid named Button. An Arm and a Leg: Anthracite has one arm broken off, presumably from a prior battle. Grayscale of Evil: Exaggerated; they (or at least Anthracite) seek to turn the whole world gray and drab. Not Always Evil: “The Necropix” introduces a cute little Necropix kid named Button, who only helps Anthracite because of some lies she made about freeing all the imprisoned Necropix. Power Floats: Anthracite is constantly levitating (this is actually a good indicator of relative power, because Ultravioletcanfly but walks unless she’s fighting, and Carmine doesn’t fly at all).

characters.name: Season Fairies
characters.description: Fog Feet: A variant; the Summer Fairy lacks legs, and instead has a jet of a flame resembling the one coming out of a rocket. Green Thumb: The Spring Fairy can grow and manipulate plants. Heel Realization: After their fighting wrecks a large tree in the park, they realize that they’re supposed to be taking care of nature, not destroying it, and figure out that winter is just as important as the other seasons. Hidden Depths: “The Half-Nymph Trial” reveals that they can each sing well- Spring sings in a theatrical style, while Summer performs pop/rap and Autumn does more chill and laid-back pop. Mushroom Man: The Autumn Fairy has a giant mushroom cap growing out of her head.

characters.name: Professor Belding
characters.description: Catchphrase: "I'm so bad!" Laughably Evil: While he can be a genuine threat at times, he pretty silly and mostly clumsy in his endeavors. Speech Impediment: Talks with a bit of a lisp in the English dub. The Rival: He declares himself as such to Toybos

characters.name: Jack Flash
characters.description: Frame-Up: He pulls this on Nate and Malika in "The Witches Convention" by making the witches think they caused a magical mishap, forcing the two to clear their names. Revenge: He focuses on trying to get revenge on the duo for stopping him the first time in "The Witches Convention". When the witches find out and thwart him, he focuses his revenge on them in "The Snowman"

characters.name: Kappa Ceti
characters.description: Disney Death:After she extinguishes herself saving Alpha Tauri, Tauri gives some light back to her, reviving her. Elmuh Fudd Syndwome: Speaks wike this. Heroic Sacrifice:Gives up the last of her light to stop Black Hole!Alpha Tauri from sucking up the Earth. Sentient Stars: A living star portrayed as a cute,Luma-esquebeing. Wish Upon a Shooting Star: When Nate sees her coming to Earth, he makes a wish.At the end of the episode, it turns out he wished to get to school on time.

characters.name: Alpha Tauri
characters.description: Heel–Face Turn:After finding out that Kappa Ceti gave up her light to save her, she understands kindness for the first time, gives some light back to Kappa, and resolves to stop sucking light from stars. Intangibility: Of a limited variety; being made of light, she can easily move through glass. Red Is Violent: Bright red, and sucks light from other stars. Sentient Stars: Like Kappa Ceti, although she’s portrayed as more of a light-basedEnergy Being. Unrealistic Black Hole: Turns into one after absorbing too much light; this form subscribes toGravity Sucks, is a flat disc, and has a “heart” rather than any sort of singularity.

characters.name: Mr. Multiply
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Typography: A living times symbol. Good All Along:Once Nate succeeds at his quiz, he drops the villain act, congratulates Nate, and comments that that really wasn’t so hard, was it? before buzzing off for a break. Monster of the Aesop: Forces Nate to answer math questions when he’s nervous about an upcoming math test. Justified, since he’s a figure in Nate’s stress dream. One-Winged Angel: Inverted; the form he takes on for his climactic showdown with Nate islessthreatening than the eye-with-two-beams-of-light that he’d previously appeared as.

characters.name: Numbers
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Typography: They appear as numerals with a number of eyes corresponding to their number. Mooks: For Mr. Multiply.

characters.name: Sigrid
characters.description: Living Drawing: A living figure from a painting.

characters.name: Monica
characters.description: Green-Eyed Monster: Steals Sigrid’s earring with hopes of becoming more beautiful, so that she’ll be hung in a place of honor instead. Living Drawing: Like Sigird, a living painting.

characters.name: Vivi
characters.description: Action Girl: Used to be one back when she was human; a flashback still shows her single-handedly facing a dragon. Elemental Embodiment: A woman made of living water. Turning Back Human: Spends most of “The Lady of the Lake” trying to find a way to break the curse… by which we mean riding around in a fishbowl while Nate and Malika attempt to find a way to break the curse. Was Once a Man: Used to be a human woman before being turned into water by a jealous wizard.

characters.name: Esther
characters.description: Alchemy Is Magic: HerRunic Magicis considered alchemy, and she’s trying to figure out how to do more impressive things like turn lead into gold. Dishing Out Dirt: All her runes seem to involve manipulating earth, whether it’s creating spikes from the ground, bringing clay to life, or even making a hole in a wall. Runic Magic: The only kind of alchemy she knows how to do is drawing magical runes.

characters.name: Golem
characters.description: Disney Death:After itsHeroic Sacrifice, Esther is able to bring it back to life by re-drawing the animating rune, although it ends up a lot smaller than before. Heroic Sacrifice:Dives into the river to save Esther from drowning, even though it knows that the water will make its clay body lose coherence. Golem: As per the myth, it’s made of clay and brought to life by a magic rune on its forehead; Esther created it as a servant, but it eventually gained its own personality and ran away. Logical Weakness: It’s made of clay, and will thus dissolve if exposed to too much water. What Measure Is a Non-Human?: Esther initially only sees it as a “soil robot”, and ordered it to do all the heavy lifting while she worked on alchemical research; she also sees nothing wrong with erasing the runes bringing it to life once it goes rogue.She eventually realizes that it’s its own being with thoughts and feelings when it sacrifices itself to save her from the river.

characters.name: Chess Pieces
characters.description: Action Girl: As per the game, the White Queen is very powerful. Malika also temporarily becomes the Black Queen for the final showdown. Dark Is Not Evil/Light Is Not Good: It’s the Black King who’s the good guy, with the White King being hell-bent on conquering real towns. Forever War: Apparently, the White and Black kings have been at war forcenturiessealed inside the chess box. This may explain why they seem to have a very limited selection of pieces at their command. Giant Board Game: They turn part of the park into a giant chessboard for their final showdown, with Nate and Malika serving as the Black King’s pieces. Logical Weakness: Despite being alive, they’re still bound by the rules of the game; the bishops can only move diagonally, while the kings in particular can only move one step at a time.

characters.name: Te Ahitia
characters.description: The Paralyzer: Anyone who touches it becomes unable to move their legs; they only become freed once it’s appeased. Red Eyes, Take Warning: When it really gets mad (due to some construction workers) and starts pouring out lava, its eyes turn bright red. Replaced with Replica: Inverted; only a replica of the tiki was supposed to be sent to Nate’s town, but somehow the real thing got shipped instead. Terrifying Tiki: Has frightening lava powers, although it’s only mad because it was shipped out of its homeland.

characters.name: Mandrake
characters.description: Cute But Cacophanous: Looks like an adorable leafy baby, but man is its screamingloud. Green Thumb: Can control other plants; this is mostly subconscious, and manifests as the plants attacking anyone who makes it scared. Innocent Plant Children: A cute little baby mandrake that’s just scared of the unfamiliar Nate and Malika. Non-Malicious Monster: He’s just a scared toddler; unfortunately, his powers mean that when he’s scared nearby plant-life will grow viciously and lash out at anyone around him.

characters.name: Dress
characters.description: Creating Life Is Unforeseen: Chloe accidentally brought it to life when she tried to use a spell to change it into her ideal wedding dress. Hereditary Wedding Dress: It was in Chloe’s family for generations… but she didn’t want to wear something so old to her wedding, so she tried to use magic to modernize it. This proved to be a bad idea. Living Clothes: Thanks to Chloe’s spell. And it can bring other clothes to life, too. Weaksauce Weakness: Water weakens the magic bringing it to life; it’s restored to inanimacy after being put in a washing machine.

characters.name: Nils
characters.description: Death Dealer: He can useUltimocards to produce real magical effects and even summon monsters. Summon Magic: CertainUltimocards can summon monsters; he calls a giant knight, and even uses Melanie as a summon (as “Melania, the Messenger of Fire”). What Measure Is a Non-Human?: He doesn’t see Melanie as a real person because she’s a magic card summon turned human. Nate and Malika are able toprove him wrongwhen he tries to send her to attack him.

characters.name: Tetsu
characters.description: Engineered Heroics: Eventually gets so desperate to repay Malika and Nate for saving him that he deliberately summons the pond’s guardian spirit (which will see them as intruders) so he can save them by un-summoning it. Kappa: Is one; he has the classic weakness to his head being spilled (although at Malika’s suggestion he puts on a helmet to keep the water in), a love of cucumbers, andmustrepay a debt. Unwanted Assistance: Nate and Malika very quickly become annoyed when he starts following them around trying to repay them.

characters.name: Francis
characters.description: Anthropomorphic Food: Another gingerbread man. Cain and Abel: He was created by Ivan to be a little brother for him, but because he wasn’t “baked with love” (Ivan didn’t know that instruction was literal) he comes out evil and starts trying to mass-produce a gingerbread army, imprisoning Ivan in the process. Heel–Face Turn: Eventually comes around to the side of good viaThe Power of Love.

characters.name: Vicky
characters.description: Cool Car: You bet your bumpers! She was awesome and practically unbeatable on the track even before she was alive. Lightning Can Do Anything: Came alive due to being struck by lightning. Nitro Boost: Can do this via a button on her dashboard; this is notably her only feature that she can’t control herself, requiring a driver to activate it. Sentient Vehicle: A racing car with a mind of her own.

characters.name: Noctis
characters.description: Bilingual Bonus: Their name is Latin for “night”. The Night That Never Ends: Their presence blocks out the sky, causing it to seem to still be night.

characters.name: Jack
characters.description: Butt-Monkey: Spends most of “The Scarecrow” being subjected toAmusing Injuriesand repeatedly shunned by Sparky. Creepy Good: He’s a creepy-looking scarecrow, but spends his time driving away darkness. Pumpkin Person: Has a pumpkin for a head. Punny Name: As in a jack-o-lantern.Becomes more apropos when he loses his lamp-on-a-stick and Sparky goes inside his pumpkin head.

characters.name: Sparky
characters.description: Logical Weakness: Being made of fire, water is dangerous to him- he’s just magical enough to withstandoneblast from Violet’s hose, but this still leaves him terribly weakened. Meaningful Name: He’s a little spark of light. The Only One: Only his light can drive away the Noctis- and only when he’s in Jack’s lantern. Trademark Favorite Food: Being made of flame, he likes to consume wood and leaves. The Unintelligible: Only Jack can understand the squeaking noises he makes, although the audience can still glean what he means pretty well from body language.

characters.name: Kikujiro
characters.description: Daruma Doll: Is one; she won’t get her other eye until the wish of her maker is granted. Heroic Sacrifice: Non-fatal variant; she gives up her second eye (both physically, and any chance of getting it back) to help stop Professor Belding. In a Single Bound: As essentially a living ball, she can jump and bounce nearly anywhere… unfortunately, since she only has one eye her aim is terrible. Obliviously Evil: Talks Professor Toybus into making a mind-reading machine, not realizing that she’s been manipulated and Professor Belding will steal it once it’s done.

characters.name: Turnip
characters.description: An Ice Person: Naturally has ice powers; Jack Flash tricks him into freezing the witches solid with his breath, and he can also move snow aroundor even pull it to his body to grow giant. Losing Your Head: Having his head come detached is an everyday occurrence for him (literally; it comes off his body whenever he hops to move), and might be a minor inconvenience if it gets knocked far away from him. Really Was Born Yesterday: He was made by Jack Flash two hours before the events of the episode. Snowlems: A cute little snowman kid.

characters.name: Tree Monster
characters.description: When Trees Attack: Starts marching on the crowd, although thanks to the kids and Turnip it never gets to actually hurt anyone.

characters.name: Soizic
characters.description: Astonishingly Appropriate Appearance: Her hair looks like a violin’s scroll, her collar has piano-key markings, and her clothes are covered in musical symbols. Evil All Along: Rather than trying to recapture a dangerous renegade, she’s just trying to pull Ronan back into a life of stifling rules. Magic Wand: Casts most of her musical spells with a conductor’s baton. Music Is Eighth Notes: HerMagic Musicconjures floating eighth notes, and sometimes uses them as attacks. Power Floats: Levitates instead of walking.

characters.name: Ronan
characters.description: Beam-O-War: In the climax of “The Pied Piper”, he shoots a blast of music from his clarinet that clashes with Soizic’s own sheet music blast. Good All Along: All he wants to do is play fun tunes, but Soizic makes him out to be a dangerous villain. Involuntary Dance: Subverted; Nate and Malika assume a dancing crowd in the park are being hypnotized by him and don headphones for protection, but when Nate’s headphones get knocked off it turns out that there was nothing magical about the tune- it was just so good that everyonewantedto dance. Magical Flautist: Technically it’s a magic instrument that resembles a clarinet, but he still fits the archetype. Power Glows: When he realizes that he can summon music from anywhere and powers up in front of a swarm of notes, the double-eighth-note on his belt glows.

characters.name: Libra and Aries
characters.description: Living Constellation: Of the Zodiac, specifically. Take My Hand!: Libra ends up saving Nate, Malika, and Aries from falling into a black hole, after being touched by Nate’s failed attempt to save Malika.

characters.name: Galatea
characters.description: Living Statue: Animated by Higgins’ gem. Non-Standard Character Design: It’s not super obvious, but her movement is jerkier and in a lower frame rate than the rest of the cartoon, evoking stop-motion aesthetics.

characters.name: Higgins
characters.description: Animating Artifact: The gem on his snake-cane can bring statues to life by touching them (if they’re peopleTaken for Granite, it even restores them to flesh-and-blood). It can also turn his snake-cane into a real snake. Karmic Transformation:After spending the whole episode trying to turn Galatea inanimate, he gets petrified by Stheno and put up on display. The Minion Master: Does no fighting himself; instead, he uses his magic gem to bring some art museum statues to life to fight for him, and later turns his snake-shaped cane into a real snake. Snakes Are Sinister: Wields a snake-shaped cane which can turn into a real snake. Taken for Granite:Ends up being petrified by Stheno after the gem is removed from his cane.

characters.name: Bonnet
characters.description: Living Hat: Comes to life due to a combination ofThe Power of HateandThe Power of Love. Make My Monster Grow: Increases in size with every bit of cloth it eats, and ends up becoming giant. Monster of the Aesop: Due to being animated by Malika’s argument with her mother (over having to wear a stupid hat, but really about her agency and personhood), it will only go back to normal if the argument is resolved. Shout-Out: In its original small and cute form, it resembles aDitto.season
